title: 6 · Methods (Deep Dive)
learn:
The story: recipe cards

A recipe card describes a job but cooks nothing until someone uses it. A method is a named block of code that does one job and only runs when called. Benefits: reuse (write once, use everywhere), organisation, easier testing, and abstraction (the caller does not need to know how it works).

Anatomy

public static int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; } Parts: modifier (public static), return type (int; void if nothing comes back), name (camelCase verb), parameters (int a, int b), body. Parameters are the placeholders in the declaration; arguments are the real values in the call: add(5, 3).

Returning values

void methods are called on their own: show(); Others hand back a value: int r = add(5, 3);. A method stops the instant it hits return, and every path through a non-void method must return something or it will not compile.

Signature

The signature is the name plus parameter list (types, number, order). It does not include the return type, modifiers or parameter names. Two methods in one class cannot share a signature.

Overloading vs overriding

Overloading: same class, same name, different parameters; chosen at compile time; changing only the return type is illegal. Overriding: subclass replaces an inherited method with the identical signature; chosen at run time. Memory trick: overLOADing = different LOAD of parameters.

Pass by value

Java always passes a copy. A primitive passed in is never changed for the caller. For an object or array the reference is copied, so the method can modify the object's contents, but reassigning its parameter does not move the caller's variable.

Scope

A variable lives only inside the braces where it is declared. Parameters and local variables vanish when the method ends. Fields (declared in the class) live as long as the object.

static vs instance

static belongs to the class: Math.sqrt(9), no object needed, and it cannot use instance fields or this. Instance methods belong to an object: s1.getGpa() needs new first.

Recursion

A method may call itself. It needs a base case that stops it, or you get StackOverflowError. Factorial: n! = n * (n-1)!, with 0! = 1.

main

public static void main(String[] args): public so the JVM can reach it, static so it runs without an object, void because it returns nothing, args holds command-line arguments.
